\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{রাজস্ব} (rājôsvô)}{রাজস্ব (rājôsvô)}]{\bn{রাজস্ব} (rājôsvô) — public revenue}

\label{lesson:BN-C348-rajosvo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to appoint, then the Bengali for to issue an order.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{রাজস্ব}}
\textbf{\bn{রাজস্ব}} — \emph{rājôsvô} — \textquotedblleft{}public revenue\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{রাজস্বের} \bn{টাকায়} \bn{নতুন} \bn{হাসপাতাল} \bn{হবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rājôsver ṭākāy nôtun hāspātāl hôbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A new hospital will be built with revenue money.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{রাজস্ব}} (\emph{rājôsvô}) is Sanskrit \emph{rājasva}, a king's own property (Monier-Williams). The sense 'public revenue' is the modern one, the state having taken the king's place.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rājôsvô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rājôsvô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rājôsver ṭākāy nôtun hāspātāl hôbe.} — A new hospital will be built with revenue money.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to appoint, then the Bengali for to issue an order, then say \emph{rājôsvô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{রাজস্ব} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Public revenue\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বাজেট} (bājeṭ)}{বাজেট (bājeṭ)}]{\bn{বাজেট} (bājeṭ) — a budget}

\label{lesson:BN-C348-bajet}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to issue an order, then the Bengali for public revenue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বাজেট}}
\textbf{\bn{বাজেট}} — \emph{bājeṭ} — \textquotedblleft{}a budget\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{এই} \bn{বছরের} \bn{বাজেটে} \bn{স্বাস্থ্যের} \bn{জন্য} \bn{কত} \bn{টাকা} \bn{আছে}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ei bôchhôrer bājeṭe svāsthyer jônyô kôtô ṭākā āchhe?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
How much money is there for health in this year's budget?
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বাজেট}} (\emph{bājeṭ}) is borrowed from English \emph{budget}, with the English vowel heard as ā.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bājeṭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bājeṭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ei bôchhôrer bājeṭe svāsthyer jônyô kôtô ṭākā āchhe?} — How much money is there for health in this year's budget?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to issue an order, then the Bengali for public revenue, then say \emph{bājeṭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{বাজেট} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A budget\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{কোষাগার} (koshāgār)}{কোষাগার (koshāgār)}]{\bn{কোষাগার} (koshāgār) — a treasury}

\label{lesson:BN-C348-koshagar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for public revenue, then the Bengali for a budget.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{কোষাগার}}
\textbf{\bn{কোষাগার}} — \emph{koshāgār} — \textquotedblleft{}a treasury\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{সরকারের} \bn{কোষাগার} \bn{এখন} \bn{খালি।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sôrkārer koshāgār ekhôn khāli.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The government's treasury is empty now.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{কোষাগার}} (\emph{koshāgār}) is Sanskrit \emph{kośāgāra}, \emph{kośa} 'a store of wealth' with \emph{āgāra} 'a house': a treasure-house (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{koshāgār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{koshāgār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sôrkārer koshāgār ekhôn khāli.} — The government's treasury is empty now.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for public revenue, then the Bengali for a budget, then say \emph{koshāgār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{কোষাগার} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A treasury\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{আদায়} \bn{করা} (ādāy kôrā)}{আদায় করা (ādāy kôrā)}]{\bn{আদায়} \bn{করা} (ādāy kôrā) — to collect dues; to get (money) out of someone}

\label{lesson:BN-C348-aday-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a budget, then the Bengali for a treasury.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{আদায়} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{আদায়} \bn{করা}} — \emph{ādāy kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to collect dues; to get (money) out of someone\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{পৌরসভা} \bn{দোকানদারদের} \bn{থেকে} \bn{ভাড়া} \bn{আদায়} \bn{করে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pourôsôbhā dokāndārder theke bhāṛā ādāy kôre.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The council collects rent from the shopkeepers.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{সব} \bn{ধার} \bn{আদায়} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini sôb dhār ādāy kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{আদায়} \bn{করা}} (\emph{ādāy kôrā}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{adāʾ}, payment or discharge, through Persian, with \bn{করা}: to make sure what is owed gets paid.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ādāy kôrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ādāy kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pourôsôbhā dokāndārder theke bhāṛā ādāy kôre.} — The council collects rent from the shopkeepers.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a budget, then the Bengali for a treasury, then say \emph{ādāy kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{মঞ্জুর} \bn{করা} (mônjur kôrā)}{মঞ্জুর করা (mônjur kôrā)}]{\bn{মঞ্জুর} \bn{করা} (mônjur kôrā) — to grant; to sanction}

\label{lesson:BN-C348-monjur-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a treasury, then the Bengali for to collect dues.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{মঞ্জুর} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{মঞ্জুর} \bn{করা}} — \emph{mônjur kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to grant; to sanction\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{সরকার} \bn{স্কুলের} \bn{জন্য} \bn{টাকা} \bn{মঞ্জুর} \bn{করল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sôrkār skuler jônyô ṭākā mônjur kôrlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The government granted money for the school.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{আমার} \bn{ছুটি} \bn{মঞ্জুর} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini āmār chhuṭi mônjur kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{মঞ্জুর} \bn{করা}} (\emph{mônjur kôrā}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{manẓūr}, 'looked at' and so approved, through Persian, with \bn{করা}: to approve a grant, a leave or a request.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mônjur kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sôrkār skuler jônyô ṭākā mônjur kôrlô.} — The government granted money for the school.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a treasury, then the Bengali for to collect dues, then say \emph{mônjur kôrā} again
\end{itemize}
